claim: >-
  Feature-local identity plus a derived product-owned inventory remains a
  reasonable direction, but the current qualification evidence cannot establish
  maintainable navigation at 1,000 modules. The common oracle also incorrectly
  rejects multiple implementation candidates for one logical module.
authority:
  accepted:
    - "ADR-0004 defines a declaration identity as (moduleId, implementationId), permits alternative implementations as separate declarations, and rejects a central module-ID registry."
    - "ADR-0006 keeps implementation IDs feature-local and permits generated inventories only for navigation and profile compilation."
    - "ADR-0007 assigns owner authority and logical owner paths to the product or repository, requires a future 1,000-declaration typecheck benchmark, and leaves the inventory format product-owned."
  proposed:
    - "ADR-0011 proposes three pre-emitter and four post-emitter edit loci; it is not accepted authority."
  nonAuthoritative:
    - "The implementation-readiness report and API fixtures are draft, disposable qualification evidence."

observedBehavior:
  - >-
    A read-only invocation of the common oracle with two declarations sharing
    moduleId "acme/search", using distinct implementation IDs and selecting only
    one candidate, returned ok:false with code "module.duplicate".
  - >-
    That behavior contradicts ADR-0004, which permits alternative
    implementations as separate declarations for one replaceable logical
    module.
  - >-
    "module.duplicate" is not in the accepted diagnostic catalog. The accepted
    related diagnostics are declaration.duplicate-implementation and
    profile.duplicate-selection.
  - >-
    The scale probe generates 10, 100, and 1,000 declarations into one scale.ts
    per candidate and records TypeScript compile duration. It does not generate
    owner-local feature files, join a package catalog, build a navigation
    inventory, or exercise add, replace, rename, move, collision, or
    go-to-source workflows.
  - >-
    The b8 navigation fixture contains two inline modules. Its own report calls
    the evidence synthetic and says inline dependencies become difficult to
    navigate at scale.
  - "The exact subject contains zero tracked files below packages/."
  - "The worktree remained clean after all reproductions."
  - >-
    The full common runner was not invoked because its final steps create
    tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/dist
    inside the read-only subject, and the local TypeScript dependency is absent.
applicability:
  appliesTo:
    - "Qualification claims about module identity, owner locality, and navigation at 1,000 modules."
    - "Maintenance workflows involving multiple implementations of one logical module."
    - "Future product-owned inventory and package-catalog integration."
  excludes:
    - "Public API selection."
    - "Runtime loading, authorization, lifecycle, or plugin behavior."
    - "Compiler graph correctness outside the reproduced identity behavior."
benefits:
  - "Feature-local identity ownership avoids a handwritten global edit hotspot."
  - "A derived inventory can provide global navigation without becoming runtime discovery or identity authority."
  - "Logical owner paths keep portable declarations independent of repository filesystem layout."
failureModes:
  - "Rejecting repeated moduleId values prevents the accepted alternative-implementation model."
  - "Maintainers may invent extra logical module IDs merely to represent replacements, increasing profile and migration complexity."
  - "A single-file typecheck can pass while cross-file discovery, ownership drift, inventory collisions, and navigation remain unusable."
  - >-
    Treating owner.path as a filesystem locator would violate the accepted
    boundary; validating syntax alone cannot prove product navigation works.
counterexamples:
  - >-
    Two declarations with moduleId "acme/search" and implementation IDs
    "acme/search/default" and "acme/search/alternate" are accepted-contract
    alternatives, yet the common oracle rejects them before profile evaluation.
  - >-
    The 1,000-declaration generator gives every declaration a unique moduleId and
    places all declarations in one file, so it never exercises the accepted
    one-module/multiple-candidate model or owner-local file navigation.

findings:
  - severity: P2
    location: >-
      tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/corpus.ts:62;
      tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/oracle.ts:45-66
    reproduction: |-
      Command:
      node --experimental-strip-types --input-type=module -e 'import { qualify } from "./tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/oracle.ts"; const a={moduleId:"acme/search",implementationId:"acme/search/default",owner:{authority:"acme",path:["search"]},provides:[],slots:[]}; const b={...a,implementationId:"acme/search/alternate"}; const world={declarations:[a,b],profile:{roots:["acme/search"],selections:[{moduleId:"acme/search",implementationId:a.implementationId}],bindings:[]}}; process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(qualify(world))+"\n")'

      Output:
      {"ok":false,"diagnostics":[{"code":"module.duplicate","path":"/modules/acme/search","detail":"acme/search"}],"inventory":["acme/search/default"],"dependencyOrder":[]}

      ADR-0004 at lines 41-53 identifies a candidate by
      (moduleId, implementationId) and explicitly permits alternative
      implementations as separate declarations. The accepted diagnostic catalog
      at lines 5-37 contains no "module.duplicate" code.
    minimalCorrection: >-
      Index declarations by implementationId and retain moduleId as a
      one-to-many logical-module membership set. Replace S21 with a positive
      two-candidate/one-selection case plus a separate duplicate profile
      selection case expecting profile.duplicate-selection. Use
      declaration.duplicate-implementation only when implementationId itself is
      repeated.
    productOwnerDecisionRequired: false
  - severity: P2
    location: >-
      tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/run.mjs:237-278;
      tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/b8/REPORT.md:22-44;
      research/implementation-readiness/report.md:340-346
    reproduction: |-
      Command:
      node --input-type=module -e 'import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; const s=readFileSync("tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/run.mjs","utf8"); const facts={sizes:/for \(const size of \[10, 100, 1000\]\)/.test(s),singleScaleFile:(s.match(/writeFileSync\(join\(directory, "scale\.ts"\)/g)||[]).length,inventoryToken:/inventory|catalog|navigate/i.test(s.slice(s.indexOf("const scaleRoot"),s.indexOf("const metrics")))}; console.log(JSON.stringify(facts))'

      Output:
      {"sizes":true,"singleScaleFile":1,"inventoryToken":false}

      The source at run.mjs:242-256 confirms that every scale case writes all
      declarations into one scale.ts and measures only compilation duration.
      "git ls-files 'packages/**' | wc -l" returned 0. ADR-0007:455-467 delegates
      navigation to a product-owned catalog join and intentionally defines no
      portable inventory format. The roadmap at lines 437-442 defers real
      navigation and edit-locus measurement to an admitted Phase 6 consumer.
    minimalCorrection: >-
      Split the report's "owner/feature locality" criterion into a Core-owned
      portable-syntax check and a product-owned navigation qualification. For
      the latter, use an admitted consumer with 1,000 owner-local module files,
      multiple implementations for representative modules, and a generated
      inventory joined to its package catalog. Measure add, replacement,
      rename/move, removal, collision diagnostics, inventory rebuild, and
      diagnostic-to-source navigation. Do not make the inventory a runtime or
      identity authority.
    productOwnerDecisionRequired: true
openQuestions:
  - >-
    Does "owner/feature locality" in the readiness report mean only portable
    owner-field syntax, or product catalog-to-source resolution? The current
    sources assign those to different owners.
  - >-
    Which admitted product or repository will allocate owner.authority and
    owner.path and define collision, rename, and stale-inventory behavior?
  - >-
    Is the scale target 1,000 logical modules or 1,000 declarations? They differ
    when one module has multiple implementation candidates.
  - >-
    What measurable navigation threshold must the Phase 6 consumer satisfy
    before identity-locality readiness is claimed?

recommendedDecision:
  disposition: NO-GO
  scope: >-
    Do not count the current common runner or b8 fixture as evidence that
    identity locality and navigation are maintainable at 1,000 modules.
  retainedDirection: >-
    Retain feature-local identities and a derived product-owned inventory,
    conditional on correcting alternative-implementation semantics and obtaining
    real consumer navigation evidence.
  productionImpact: >-
    This is a qualification-only conclusion; it does not select a public API or
    authorize production source.
